questions.question: A sum of Rs. 150 is divided into two parts. The first part is Rs. 2 more than three times the second part. Find the second part.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rs 150 is divided into two parts.

First part is Rs 2 more than three times the second part.

**Calculation:**

Let the second part of the division from Rs 150 be x.

First part = 3x + 2

Now, equating it to 150, we get

⇒ x + 3x + 2 = 150

⇒ 4x = 148

⇒ x = 148 ÷ 4 = 37

**Therefore, the second part is Rs 37.**

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it amount to 9 times of itself?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years.

**Concept Used:**

Amount = P(1+(r)/(100))^n

**Calculation:**

When the sum of money gets tripled in 10 years,

Amount = 3P

⇒ 3P = P(1+(r)/(100))¹⁰

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))¹⁰ = (3P)/(P) = 3 → (1)

Now, when the amount required is 9 times of itself,

Amount = 9P

⇒ 9P = P(1+(r)/(100))^n

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = (9P)/(P) = 9 = 3² → (2)

Putting the value of 3 from equation (1) into equation (2), we get

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = ({(1+(r)/(100))}¹⁰)²

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = (1+(r)/(100))¹⁰times ²

Equating the powers, we get

⇒ n = 20 years

**Therefore, the required time in which the amount becomes 9 times of itself is 20 years.**

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 205. If one of these numbers is reduced by 5% and the other is increased by 10%, the resulting numbers are equal to each other. Find the smaller of the two initial numbers.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 205

First number reduced by = 5%

Second number increased by = 10%

Resulting numbers are equal to each other.

**Calculation:**

Let the numbers be x and y.

⇒ x + y = 205

⇒ x = 205 – y → (1)

⇒ First number after reduction = x – (5)/(100)times x = (20x-x)/(20) = (19x)/(20)

⇒ Second number after increase = y + (10)/(100)times y = (10y+y)/(10) = (11y)/(10)

According to the question,

⇒ (19x)/(20)=(11y)/(10)

⇒ 19x = 22y

⇒ x = (22y)/(19)

Putting this value in equation (1), we get

⇒ (22y)/(19) = 205 – y

⇒ (22y)/(19) + y = 205

⇒ 22y + 19y = 205 × 19

⇒ 41y = 205 × 19

⇒ y = (205times 19)/(41) = 95

⇒ x = 205 – 95 = 110

**Therefore, the smallest of the two initial numbers is 95.**

Now, 15 years ago

Mother's age = x – 15

Son's age = y – 15

⇒ x = 2y – 15 → (2)

⇒ y = 30 + 15 = 45

Present age of mother = x = 30 + 45 = 75

**Therefore, the present age of mother is 75 years.**

questions.question: Which of the following acid-base pairs will produce a salt of ammonium chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HCl - NH4OH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **three major classifications** of substances known as acids or bases. The Arrhenius definition states that an acid **produces H+** in solution and a **base produces OH-**. 
 
• This theory was developed by **Svante Arrhenius in 1883**. Later, two more sophisticated and general theories were proposed.
 
• In 1884, the Swedish chemist **Svante Arrhenius** proposed two specific classifications of compounds; **acids and bases**.
 
• An Arrhenius acid is a compound that increases the **concentration of H+** ions that are present when added to water. These H+ ions form the **hydronium ion (H3O+)** when they combine with water molecules. This process is represented in a chemical equation by adding H2O to the reactants side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acids and bases are** important compounds in the natural world**, so their chemistry is central to any discussion of chemical reactions. There are several theories of acid-base behaviour.
 
• The Arrhenius theory, named after **Swedish physicist Svante August Arrhenius**, views an acid as a substance that increases the concentration of the hydronium ion (H3O+) in an aqueous solution and a base as a substance that increases the hydroxide ion (OH−) concentration.
 
• According to the** Arrhenius theory**, acid-base reactions involve the combination of the hydrogen ion (H+) and the hydroxide ion to form water. 
 
• A somewhat more general acid-base theory, the **Brønsted-Lowry theory**, named after** Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted **and English **chemist Thomas Martin Lowry**, defines an acid as **a proton donor** and** a base as a proton acceptor**.
